BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team
**Status:** Buyer-side working analysis. Seller statements of "agreed", "settled", "adequate" or "not expected to be material" are treated as assertions only (playbook 0.4/6.3) and have not been accepted as fact.

## Headline view

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced"; it departs from our playbook on essentially every point and, read as a whole, it collapses the separate Title/Fundamental, Tax and IP regimes into a 20%-capped, 18-month, disclosure-and-knowledge-qualified general regime with no fraud carve-out. The Disclosure Letter is actually helpful to us: it candidly confirms that Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment, Ironquay payment/assignment and bonus funding are all **not** done. Several of our pushbacks are therefore grounded in the Seller's own admissions, not just our preferences.

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### 1. General warranty cap (cl 12.1) – 20% / AUD 4.8m
**Departure.** Our position is 25% / AUD 6.0m. The Seller's number coincides with our conditional fallback, but the fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given. A number matching a fallback is not clearance.
**Push back:** Hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal that 20% is reachable.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)
**Departure on all three elements:**
- De minimis AUD 25,000 (ours: 5,000) – 5x our position.
- Basket AUD 250,000 (ours: 50,000) – 5x our position.
- Excess-only recovery (ours: first dollar once exceeded).
Combined with the knowledge bar and general disclosure, this would make most mid-sized claims uneconomic to bring.
**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping (first-dollar) basket.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3/13) – 18 months, "all limitations apply to all Claims"
**Departure.** 18 months is our fallback; no Amelia Frost approval exists. More importantly, the second sentence – "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" – is a hidden general-regime override. It would sweep Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment covenants and leakage claims into the 18-month/20%/basket regime unless we spot and carve out each one.
**Push back:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the opposite: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended. Build a limitations table showing each category separately.

### 4. Fundamental / Title warranties
**Departure.** Seller wants capacity and title under general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity". That is not a legitimate rationale; it is a transfer of 100% title risk to the Buyer for a AUD 24m price with a AUD 4.8m ceiling.
**Push back:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside de minimis, basket, disclosure and knowledge bar.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) – "all Claims of any nature"
**Departure – critical.** No carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct. As drafted, a fraudulently concealed matter would be capped at 20%, time-barred at 18 months, and subject to non-reliance. This is a non-negotiable for us and in any event unlikely to be enforced in NSW for fraud, but we must not leave it to the court.
**Push back:** Express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. Non-reliance must not extend to the Warranties, Disclosure Letter or specific indemnities themselves.

### 6. Disclosure (Sch 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
**Departure.** Whole-data-room (DD-002 to DD-012, as at 22 Sept 2026) and public-register deemed disclosure. This is exactly what the playbook rejects. Note the Letter's own standard in para 11 ("the Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts") effectively puts the burden of discovering problems on us.
**Push back:** Disclosure only of matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; delete 1.1 and 1.2 general disclosure of the data room and public records; retain only specific, numbered disclosures against identified warranties. Require a bring-down and no new disclosure between signing and Completion without our consent.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
**Departure.** Blanket exclusion for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew "or discoverable from the data room or public records". "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that would gut the warranties. It also runs the wrong way: knowledge qualifiers belong to seller warranties, not buyer claims.
**Push back:** Delete 8.3 entirely. If any knowledge qualifier survives in seller warranties, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
**Departure – material.** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. Seller offers only reasonable endeavours and deems the condition satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. "Addressed" in the Seller Update is not a status; it is a characterisation.
**Push back:** Condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent under cl 11.2, and (b) documentary evidence that each 11.3 condition has been met, in each case before Completion and in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer. Seller to use all reasonable endeavours (not merely reasonable). Consider a Bluefen-specific indemnity / price protection if consent is obtained on terms that alter the contract.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7) – ~AUD 3.2m
**Departure – material.** Post-completion release. Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is in the data room. On a debt-free basis we would be buying a company with AUD 3.2m of bank debt and live security, relying on a promise of a later release, with change-of-control (8.1) potentially triggered at Completion.
**Push back:** Current payout letter (dated no earlier than 2 business days pre-Completion), repayment directly out of Completion funds on the funds flow, and executed releases/discharges of all security (including PPSR and any share mortgage/guarantees) delivered at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval – neither exists.

### 10. Employee bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000
**Departure.** Funds flow "reflects agreed price mechanics" (nothing is agreed) and the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent from the funds flow and is silent on superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs. In practice the Company – i.e. us – pays these after Completion unless funded.
**Push back:** Specific line item in the funds flow: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (SG, payroll tax, any leave accrual effects), either paid by the Seller pre-Completion or deducted as Debt/Transaction Bonuses from the price. Require a schedule of recipients, conditions and gross-up calculations.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
**Departure.** Indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment and declared "adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4 confirms: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 shows as open on DD-010 (not bank-verified either way); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room. The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables.
**Push back:** Preserve the cure path: require payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees (whatever the verified amount is) and a confirmatory IP assignment/receipt from Ironquay before Completion, Seller-funded. Broaden the indemnity to cover any loss from the Company not holding title to, or any third-party claim in respect of, SOW3 Project Materials, outside the general cap/basket/time limits. Treat AUD 180,000 as unverified; obtain bank evidence.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
**Departure in characterisation, not necessarily substance.** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" is an assertion. Disclosure Letter para 6 confirms ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address, with access, scope and notification obligations undetermined. Consistent with the playbook we do **not** assume a breach, harm, notification duty or any number – but equally we do not accept the Seller's non-materiality.
**Push back:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, complete and document the investigation (including access-attempt data for the link), provide weekly updates and final report, and take any required regulatory/individual notifications before Completion on advice. Specific warranty that the disclosure is complete; a specific indemnity for costs and liabilities arising from this incident, outside the general regime, is reasonable to request. Do not let DD-006 be "disclosed" generally against the privacy/data warranties.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011) – AUD 330,000
**Assessment only.** "Ordinary-course operating costs" is an assertion; the Letter admits it does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Per playbook, no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
**Action:** Request the three renewal documents, timing, termination rights and accruals; decide treatment (ordinary course vs accrued liability in working capital/Debt) once facts are in.

### 14. Tax / IP
**Departure.** "Settled under the general regime" – not agreed, and the Seller's regime wording (item 3 above) would absorb them. Playbook: terms remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution.
**Push back:** Record Tax and IP as open; maintain separate categories with their own caps and periods (tax period to follow statutory amendment periods at minimum); no general-regime override.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Departure.** Title "evidenced by the Company share register". Disclosure Letter para 10 itself concedes this is only the source the Seller relies on and that the Buyer has not verified it. An internal register is not independent proof.
**Push back:** Obtain ASIC current and historical extracts, PPSR search, Riverlark security documents (any share mortgage), constitution, share certificates, board minutes/transfer history and evidence of Harbourglass's authority (board approvals, signatory capacity). Title and authority warranties to sit in the Fundamental regime (item 4).

### 16. Residual points
- **Disclosure Letter 1.4 / 11:** non-admission and "no conclusion" reservations are standard but reinforce that nothing in the Letter should be read as the Seller conceding any of the above; conversely, nothing in it binds us either.
- **Office lease (DD-007) / Mossvale (DD-009):** both appear to be notification/assignment provisions rather than change-of-control consents. Verify wording ourselves; require pre-Completion notifications where applicable and a warranty that no other consents are required.
- **Seller Update generally:** phrases such as "agreed price mechanics", "is addressed", "considered adequate" and "settled" have no evidentiary or contractual weight and should be expressly rejected in our cover note so no course of dealing is implied.

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Topic | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | 25% / 6.0m; no fallback authority exists |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess-only | 5k / 50k / first dollar |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months; limits apply to all Claims | 24 months; delete universal-application clause; separate limitations table |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge/disclosure |
| 5 | Fraud carve-out | None | Carve fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct out of everything |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public records | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; deemed satisfied on delivery | CP: effective consent + evidence conditions satisfied pre-Completion |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised; "Seller matter" | Line item: 420k + on-costs, seller-funded or price deduction |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3-payment-only indemnity | Pay and obtain assignment pre-Completion; broaden indemnity; verify 180k |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Log preservation, investigation, updates, specific warranty/indemnity; no assumption either way |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess on documents; no automatic treatment |
| 14 | Tax/IP | "Settled" under general regime | Open; separate regimes |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence |

**Priority order for the mark-up and cover note:** (i) fraud carve-out and the "applies to all Claims" override; (ii) Fundamental/Title separate regime and independent title evidence; (iii) Bluefen and Riverlark conditions, because the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms neither is done; (iv) cap/thresholds/time; (v) disclosure and knowledge; (vi) bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006 as specific line items/indemnities; (vii) Tax/IP and Sandbar flagged as open.

Nothing in the Seller's package is cleared on our side; no Amelia Frost authority should be assumed or sought on the basis of this draft alone. If the team wants to explore the 20%/18-month fallbacks, that is a separate internal decision to be documented through our authority process before anything is signalled to Harbourglass.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011) – AUD 330,000
**Assessment only.** "Ordinary-course operating costs" is an assertion; the Letter admits it does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. Per playbook, no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

### 14. Tax / IP
**Departure.** "Settled under the general regime" – not agreed, and the Seller's regime wording (item 3 above) would absorb them. Playbook: terms remain OPEN; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution.
**Push back:** Record Tax and IP as open; maintain separate categories with their own caps and periods (tax period to follow statutory amendment periods at minimum); no general-regime override.

### 15. Title evidence (DD-012)
**Departure.** Title "evidenced by the Company share register". Disclosure Letter para 10 itself concedes this is only the source the Seller relies on and that the Buyer has not verified it. An internal register is not independent proof.
**Push back:** Obtain ASIC current and historical extracts, PPSR search, Riverlark security documents (any share mortgage), constitution, share certificates, board minutes/transfer history and evidence of Harbourglass's authority (board approvals, signatory capacity). Title and authority warranties to sit in the Fundamental regime (item 4).

### 16. Residual points
- **Disclosure Letter 1.4 / 11:** non-admission and "no conclusion" reservations are standard but reinforce that nothing in the Letter should be read as the Seller conceding any of the above; conversely, nothing in it binds us either.
- **Office lease (DD-007) / Mossvale (DD-009):** both appear to be notification/assignment provisions rather than change-of-control consents. Verify wording ourselves; require pre-Completion notifications where applicable and a warranty that no other consents are required.
- **Seller Update generally:** phrases such as "agreed price mechanics", "is addressed", "considered adequate" and "settled" have no evidentiary or contractual weight and should be expressly rejected in our cover note so no course of dealing is implied.
